cards.explanation: The answer is that Amos is accused of conspiring against the king. Amaziah sends word to Jeroboam, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel." Amaziah is the priest of Bethel, and Jeroboam is Israel's king. He sent word to the king, friends, and I think that tells you a lot.

The answer is by the sword. Amaziah reports that Amos said, "Jeroboam will die by the sword…" That's Amaziah's report of the words, and I'll tell you, it's not the kind of news a king wants delivered by messenger. Amaziah also says it's why the land can't bear Amos's words.

The word is exile. Amaziah says Amos claimed, "…Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland." Exile means being taken out of your own land. Amaziah is the one reporting it, so these are the words as he tells them to the king.

The answer is Judah. Amaziah says, "Flee to the land of Judah; earn your bread there and do your prophesying there." Judah is where Amaziah wants Amos to go, friends. He's very sure about the travel plans.

The reason is that Bethel is the king's sanctuary. Amaziah says, "…because it is the sanctuary of the king and the temple of the kingdom." Bethel is what he's talking about. Amos is told to take his prophesying somewhere else.

The answer is False. Amos says, "I was not a prophet…" and adds that he wasn't the son of a prophet either. He was "…a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees." He tells Amaziah where he really came from, friends.

The answer is the LORD. Amos says, "But the LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’" Amos wasn't sent by a king or a priest. His answer to Amaziah is all about who sent him.

The answer is False. Amos says, "Now, therefore, hear the word of the LORD. You say: ‘Do not prophesy against Israel…’" The "you" is Amaziah, and the word that follows is for him, friends. Jeroboam isn't the one being spoken to.
The word is divided. The LORD says to Amaziah, "Your land will be divided by a measuring line…" A measuring line is for marking out portions of land. That's what the LORD says about Amaziah's land.

The answer is True. The LORD says to Amaziah, "…and you yourself will die on pagan soil." It's part of the word Amos delivers in 7:17. The priest who told Amos to go away hears about his own end, friends.
